title: xAI Adds Character References and Teases 1080p for Grok Imagine Video
excerpt: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 now supports multi-image character references for consistent subjects across clips, while app code reveals an upcoming 1080p upscale option for the AI video generator.
body:
• Grok Imagine now supports up to seven reference images per video generation, allowing creators to maintain consistent characters, styles, and environments across clips.
  • The Video 1.5 update, built on xAI's Aurora autoregressive engine, generates 6-second 720p clips in approximately 25 seconds with native synchronized audio.
  • App researcher Nima Owji spotted an "Upscale to 1080p" feature in the Grok app code, with Elon Musk responding "Try it out"—suggesting a full HD option is imminent.
  • Grok Imagine Video 1.5 topped the LMSYS Image-to-Video Arena leaderboard upon release, priced at $0.14 per second via API—roughly 86% below Sora's pricing before its deprecation.

Multi-Image References Change the Workflow

xAI has rolled out character reference support for Grok Imagine, its AI video generation platform available through X and the Grok API. The feature allows creators to upload up to seven reference images per generation, enabling the system to lock characters, objects, and stylistic elements across multiple clips.

https://x.com/rohanpaul_ai/status/2083545533248070070

The multi-reference capability addresses one of the most persistent frustrations in AI video: maintaining visual consistency. Previously, each new generation risked producing a slightly different version of the same character, making multi-shot storytelling impractical. With the update, users can tag images using an "@image" syntax in their prompts, specifying which reference should inform the character, background, or props in the output.

A phased rollout that began in mid-March 2026 has now reached general availability. The feature is powered by xAI's Aurora model, which processes frames sequentially, conditioning each new frame on all prior frames to maintain temporal coherence.

"The multi-image reference feature entered phased rollout in mid-March 2026, gradually granting more users access to the multi-picker interface for improved character and object locking across motion sequences."

— Grokipedia documentation

Video 1.5: Faster, Longer, With Native Audio

The character reference update arrives alongside Grok Imagine Video 1.5, which xAI released to general availability in June 2026 after a preview period. The model generates clips of up to 15 seconds at 480p or 720p resolution, with audio—including dialogue, ambient sound, and music—produced natively in the same generation pass.

The "Fast" tier cuts generation time by roughly 40%, producing a 6-second, 720p video in about 25 seconds. The engine runs on Aurora, trained on a cluster of 110,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs, and outputs H.264 MP4 at 24 frames per second across multiple aspect ratios.

On the LMSYS Image-to-Video Arena leaderboard, Grok Imagine Video 1.5 holds the top position by Elo ranking, ahead of ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 and Kuaishou's Kling 2.6. Its API pricing of $4.20 per minute at 720p undercuts most competitors, including the now-deprecated Sora 2 Pro, which charged $30 per minute for 1080p output.

1080p Is Coming—But Not Quite Here

The most anticipated upgrade remains resolution. Grok Imagine Video currently caps at 720p, which suffices for social media and rapid prototyping but falls short of broadcast and professional standards where 1080p is baseline.

In April 2026, app researcher Nima Owji discovered an "Upscale to 1080p" option in the Grok app's code. When he posted the finding on X, the post drew over 58,700 views. Musk responded with "Try it out," strongly suggesting the feature was in testing.

Whether xAI implements native 1080p generation or an upscaling approach matters technically—native rendering produces sharper detail, while upscaling a 720p source can appear smoothed. Aurora's sequential architecture makes native 1080p computationally expensive: each frame's token count increases by roughly 2.25 times, extending the generation chain proportionally.

The Competitive Landscape

xAI's video push comes as OpenAI winds down Sora, with the consumer app discontinued in April 2026 and the Sora 2 API sunsetting in September 2026. Google's Veo 3.1 offers 1080p but at significantly higher cost. ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 supports 1080p with music beat synchronization but takes up to 12 mixed assets per generation.

For Indian-origin creators and tech professionals—a growing segment of the AI-tools market—Grok Imagine's aggressive pricing and X integration offer a low-barrier entry point for social content, marketing, and creative experimentation.

What's Next

xAI has outlined ambitious targets: 30-minute video content by late 2026 and full-length films in 2027. Elon Musk revealed in April that the next-generation Imagine V2 model is training on SpaceXAI's Colossus 2 infrastructure. More immediately, the 1080p option and further refinements to audio quality and prompt adherence are expected in the coming weeks.
nri_angle: Indian-origin creators and tech professionals can leverage Grok Imagine's aggressive API pricing as a low-barrier entry point for AI-generated social content and marketing.
